# libtmux for Perl Drive tmux from Perl: [create sessions][server-new-session], [type into panes][server-send-text], and [filter what tmux holds][selection-where] with ordinary arrays. [![Perl checks](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-perl/actions/workflows/scaffold.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-perl/actions/workflows/scaffold.yml) [![LibTmux](https://img.shields.io/cpan/v/LibTmux?label=LibTmux)](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux) [![libtmux.org](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-libtmux.org-0b7285)](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-perl/blob/master/LICENSE)
The core needs only the Perl standard library at runtime. Async and workspace ship as separate packages under [Choose a package](#choose-a-package). Install the core with [cpm](https://github.com/skaji/cpm): ```console $ cpm install \ --global \ LibTmux ``` It needs: - **Perl 5.44 or newer.** - **tmux 3.3a or newer.** - **Linux on x86-64, including WSL.** See [compatibility](docs/compatibility.md). The `0.x` API can change between releases. Each distribution's `Changes` file marks the breaks; pin a version in applications. **Contents** — [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Find things](#find-sessions-windows-and-panes) · [Send input](#send-input-and-run-commands) · [Plan a query](#plan-a-query) · [Packages](#choose-a-package) · [Examples](#run-the-examples-and-read-the-guides) · [Leaves out](#what-it-leaves-out) · [Support](#support-and-status) [Documentation](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/guides/) · [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/reference/) · [CPAN](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux) ## Quick start ### [`Server->new_session`][server-new-session]: create a session and arrange its windows Create a session, [split its window][server-split-pane], [resize the new pane][server-resize-pane], add another window, and read the result. The program runs its own tmux server and removes it on exit: ```perl use v5.44; use File::Temp (); use LibTmux::Server; # Without a socket argument, a private temporary directory holds the server. my $private = File::Temp->newdir('libtmux-perl-XXXXXX', TMPDIR => 1); my $socket = shift @ARGV // "$private/tmux.sock"; my $server = LibTmux::Server->new( socket_path => $socket, executable => shift(@ARGV) // 'tmux', config_file => '/dev/null', ); my ($session, $snapshot, $side, $failure); try { $session = $server->new_session( name => 'perl-quickstart', command => [$^X, '-e', 'while () { print }'], ); my $editor = $session->window_links->one->window; $server->rename_window(window => $editor, name => 'editor'); $side = $server->split_pane( pane => $editor->panes->one, horizontal => true, command => [$^X, '-e', 'while () { print }'], ); $server->resize_pane(pane => $side, width => 20); $server->new_window( session => $session, name => 'logs', command => [$^X, '-e', 'while () { print }'], ); $snapshot = $server->snapshot; } catch ($error) { $failure = $error; $session //= $error->created if $error isa LibTmux::X::Creation; } if ($session) { try { $server->kill_session(session => $session) } catch ($cleanup) { warn "session cleanup failed: $cleanup\n"; $failure //= $cleanup; } } die $failure if defined $failure; # The captured graph remains readable after its live session has gone. for my $link ($snapshot->session_by_id($session->id)->window_links->@*) { my $count = $link->window->panes->count; say $link->window->name, ': ', $count, $count == 1 ? ' pane' : ' panes'; } say 'side pane: ', $snapshot->pane_by_id($side->id)->width, ' columns'; ``` It prints: ```text editor: 2 panes logs: 1 pane side pane: 20 columns ``` To run it, save it as `quickstart.pl`: ```console $ perl quickstart.pl ``` [`Server`][server] owns every command, and `new_session` starts tmux when none is running. The captured [`Snapshot`][snapshot] stays readable after its session is gone. [`kill_session`][server-kill-session], [`kill_window`][server-kill-window], [`kill_pane`][server-kill-pane] and [`kill_server`][server-kill-server] remove what you created. Pass a socket path to join a server of your own: the program then removes only the session it created, and an existing session with the same name is an error. More: [orchestration guide](docs/orchestration.md). ## Find sessions, windows and panes ### [`Selection->where`][selection-where]: filter with criteria and Perl callbacks A [`Selection`][selection] is a blessed array reference: `where`, `grep` and `map` chain without another tmux call. ```perl use v5.44; use File::Temp (); use LibTmux::Server; my $private = File::Temp->newdir('libtmux-perl-XXXXXX', TMPDIR => 1); my $server = LibTmux::Server->new( socket_path => "$private/tmux.sock", config_file => '/dev/null', ); my $failure; try { my $session = $server->new_session( name => 'perl-select', command => [$^X, '-e', 'while () { print }'], ); my $editor = $session->window_links->one->window; $server->rename_window(window => $editor, name => 'editor'); $server->split_pane( pane => $editor->panes->one, horizontal => true, command => [$^X, '-e', 'while () { print }'], ); my $snapshot = $server->snapshot; my $panes = $snapshot->windows->one({name => 'editor'}) ->panes->where({width => {-gte => 1}}) ->grep(sub ($pane) { $pane->height > 0 }); my $active = $panes->one({active => true}); say 'editor panes: ', $panes->count; say 'active pane belongs to ', $active->window->name; # example: begin nomatch try { $panes->one({width => {-gt => 10_000}}) } catch ($error) { die $error unless $error isa LibTmux::X::NoMatch; say 'no pane is that wide'; } # example: end nomatch } catch ($error) { $failure = $error } # The server is private, so stopping it removes everything the program made. try { $server->kill_server } catch ($error) { $failure //= $error unless $error isa LibTmux::X::NoServer } die $failure if defined $failure; ``` It prints: ```text editor panes: 2 active pane belongs to editor no pane is that wide ``` `one` throws on none or several matches; `one_or_undef` returns undef for none. More: [filtering guide](docs/filtering.md). ### [`LibTmux::Filter`][filter]: save a reusable filter A [`Filter`][filter] compiles criteria once, matches plain hash records without tmux, and round-trips through versioned JSON: ```perl use v5.44; use LibTmux::Filter; my $filter = LibTmux::Filter->new( entity => 'pane', where => { active => true, current_command => {-in => [qw(perl vim)]}, width => {-gte => 80}, }, ); my @records = ( {id => '%1', active => true, current_command => 'perl', width => 120}, {id => '%2', active => false, current_command => 'perl', width => 120}, {id => '%3', active => true, current_command => 'vim', width => 40}, ); my @matches = grep { $filter->matches($_) } @records; say 'matching records: ', join ', ', map { $_->{id} } @matches; ``` It prints `matching records: %1`. Save and restore it: ```perl my $restored = LibTmux::Filter->from_json($filter->to_json); say 'restored filter matches: ', scalar grep { $restored->matches($_) } @records; ``` It prints `restored filter matches: 1`. Regular expressions work in callbacks, not in the JSON. More: [filtering guide](docs/filtering.md). ## Send input and run commands ### [`Server->send_text`][server-send-text]: send text, capture output, and set environment [`send_text`][server-send-text] types literal text and [`send_keys`][server-send-keys] takes tmux key names. [`capture_pane`][server-capture-pane] reads the screen, and [`set_option`][server-set-option] and [`get_option`][server-get-option] read and write options: ```perl use v5.44; use File::Temp (); use LibTmux::Server; my $private = File::Temp->newdir('libtmux-perl-XXXXXX', TMPDIR => 1); my $server = LibTmux::Server->new( socket_path => "$private/tmux.sock", config_file => '/dev/null', ); my $failure; try { my $session = $server->new_session( name => 'perl-input', command => [$^X, '-e', 'while () { print }'], ); my $pane = $session->window_links->one->window->panes->one; $server->send_text( pane => $pane, text => 'hello from Perl', enter => true ); print $server->capture_pane(pane => $pane, start => -100) =~ s/\n+\z/\n/r; $server->set_environment( session => $session, name => 'PROJECT', value => 'api', ); say 'PROJECT=', $server->get_environment(session => $session, name => 'PROJECT'); my %build = (scope => 'session', target => $session->id, name => '@build'); $server->set_option(%build, value => 'ok'); say '@build=', $server->get_option(%build); # example: begin batch my $batch = $server->batch( [ ['display-message', '-p', '-t', $pane->id, '#{session_name}'], ['display-message', '-p', '-t', $pane->id, '#{pane_index}'], ] ); for my $entry ($batch->@*) { die $entry->{error} if defined $entry->{error}; print $entry->{result}->stdout; } # example: end batch } catch ($error) { $failure = $error } # The server is private, so stopping it removes everything the program made. try { $server->kill_server } catch ($error) { $failure //= $error unless $error isa LibTmux::X::NoServer } die $failure if defined $failure; ``` It prints: ```text hello from Perl hello from Perl PROJECT=api @build=ok perl-input 0 ``` Tmux accepting a command does not mean the pane finished. Capture again until the screen shows what you expect. [`set_hook`][server-set-hook] and [`show_hooks`][server-show-hooks] write and read hooks. More: [orchestration guide](docs/orchestration.md). ### [`Server->batch`][server-batch]: run several commands, keep each result [`batch`][server-batch] takes argv arrays and returns one `{result, error}` record per command, in order. A failing command does not stop the rest. ```perl my $batch = $server->batch( [ ['display-message', '-p', '-t', $pane->id, '#{session_name}'], ['display-message', '-p', '-t', $pane->id, '#{pane_index}'], ] ); for my $entry ($batch->@*) { die $entry->{error} if defined $entry->{error}; print $entry->{result}->stdout; } ``` It prints the session name and the pane index: `perl-input`, then `0`. More: [orchestration guide](docs/orchestration.md). ## Plan a query ### [`Server->explain_panes`][server-explain-panes]: see what runs in tmux and what stays local [`explain_panes`][server-explain-panes] builds a [`QueryPlan`][queryplan] without any I/O. [`query_panes`][server-query-panes] runs the same criteria against tmux. Its `pushdown` switch is `auto`, `never` or `require`. ```perl use v5.44; use LibTmux::Server; # Planning does no I/O, so this program needs no tmux server. my $server = LibTmux::Server->new; my $criteria = {active => true, width => {-gte => 1}}; my $plan = $server->explain_panes(where => $criteria); say 'tmux filter: ', $plan->to_data->{native_filter}; my $relation = {window => {-is => {name => 'editor'}}}; my $residual = $server->explain_panes(where => $relation); say 'stays local: ', $residual->to_data->{residual_reasons}[0]; my $never = $server->explain_panes(where => $criteria, pushdown => 'never'); say 'pushdown off: ', $never->summary; ``` It prints: ```text tmux filter: #{&&:#{==:#{pane_active},1},#{e|>=:#{pane_width},1}} stays local: window requires local relation, byte, null, or unavailable-field semantics pushdown off: local evaluation; pushdown disabled ``` Perl always computes the result; tmux only double-checks what it can express. More: [query planning guide](docs/query-planning.md). ## Choose a package | Distribution | Use it for | Package and API | | --- | --- | --- | | [LibTmux](packages/core/README.md) | Commands, snapshots, graph navigation, filtering, options and environment. | [CPAN](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux) · [API](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/reference/) · [POD](https://metacpan.org/pod/LibTmux) | | [LibTmux-Async](packages/async/README.md) | Concurrent Future-returning operations and explicit executor cleanup. | [CPAN](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux-Async) · [API](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/reference/libtmux-async-server/) · [POD](https://metacpan.org/pod/LibTmux::Async) | | [LibTmux-Workspace](packages/workspace/README.md) | Validate, plan, and load JSON workspaces with a library or CLI. | [CPAN](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux-Workspace) · [API](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/workspace/reference/libtmux-workspace/) · [POD](https://metacpan.org/pod/LibTmux::Workspace) | Companions install by module name, and cpm adds the core for you: ```console $ cpm install \ --global \ LibTmux::Async ``` ```console $ cpm install \ --global \ LibTmux::Workspace ``` ### [`LibTmux`](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-perl/tree/master/packages/core): the library [`Server`](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/reference/libtmux-server/) commands, [`Snapshot`](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/reference/libtmux-snapshot/) graphs, and [`Selection`](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/reference/libtmux-selection/) filters. [![LibTmux](https://img.shields.io/cpan/v/LibTmux?label=LibTmux)](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux) [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/reference/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/guides/) · [CPAN](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux) · [POD](https://metacpan.org/pod/LibTmux) · [Changes](packages/core/Changes) ### [`LibTmux-Async`](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-perl/tree/master/packages/async): Futures on a caller-owned loop [`LibTmux::Async::Server`](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/reference/libtmux-async-server/) runs the core operations as Futures and awaits its executor's cleanup. [![LibTmux-Async](https://img.shields.io/cpan/v/LibTmux-Async?label=LibTmux-Async)](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux-Async) [Guide](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/guides/async/) · [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/reference/libtmux-async-server/) · [CPAN](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux-Async) · [POD](https://metacpan.org/pod/LibTmux::Async) · [Changes](packages/async/Changes) ### [`LibTmux-Workspace`](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-perl/tree/master/packages/workspace): JSON workspaces, with a CLI [`LibTmux::Workspace`](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/workspace/reference/libtmux-workspace/) and the `libtmux-workspace` command validate, plan, and load a workspace file. [![LibTmux-Workspace](https://img.shields.io/cpan/v/LibTmux-Workspace?label=LibTmux-Workspace)](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux-Workspace) [Guide](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/workspace/source-guide/) · [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/workspace/reference/) · [CPAN](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux-Workspace) · [POD](https://metacpan.org/pod/LibTmux::Workspace) · [Changes](packages/workspace/Changes) ## Run the examples and read the guides [The examples index](examples/README.md) lists every runnable program. Run them all from a checkout: ```console $ mise exec -- make examples ``` - [Installation](docs/installation.md): from CPAN or a checkout - [Orchestration](docs/orchestration.md): create, arrange, type, capture - [Filtering](docs/filtering.md): criteria, quantifiers, wire format - [Graph identity](docs/graph.md): snapshots and linked windows - [Query planning](docs/query-planning.md): what tmux runs and what stays local - [Async execution](docs/async.md): Futures on your own loop - [Workspace loading](docs/workspace.md): JSON workspaces and the CLI - [Errors and recovery](docs/errors.md): typed exceptions - [Compatibility](docs/compatibility.md): supported platforms Installed API documentation uses POD: ```console $ perldoc LibTmux::Server ``` ## What it leaves out - **Control mode.** No persistent connection or subscriptions. - **Command chaining.** `batch` makes separate tmux calls, not one command list. - **Serialized regexes.** Regular expressions work in callbacks only. - **Relation pushdown.** Relation criteria are always checked in Perl. ## Support and status - **The `0.x` API can change.** Read each `Changes` file before upgrading. - **Standard library at runtime.** Async adds Future, IO::Async and IO::Ppoll. - **Linux on x86-64, including WSL.** Other systems are untested. [Contributing](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) covers author setup and checks. [Perl choices](.github/PERL.md) records dependency decisions, [architecture decisions](docs/dev/adr/index.md) explain the contracts, and [branding](docs/branding.md) describes the logos and social cards. ---
title: Install Perl packages
description: Install the independent Perl core, async, and workspace distributions.
---

Needs Perl 5.44 or newer, tmux 3.3a or newer, and Linux on x86-64, including
WSL. Install the packages you need from CPAN, or use a source checkout for
development. The [documentation homepage](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/) links
the guides and [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/perl/latest/reference/).

## Install from CPAN

Install [Perl](https://www.perl.org/get.html) and
[cpm](https://github.com/skaji/cpm#installation), then use one interpreter and
installation prefix for every package.

Install [LibTmux](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux) for commands, snapshots,
and filtering:

```console
$ cpm install \
    --global \
    LibTmux
```

Add [LibTmux-Workspace](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux-Workspace) for the
JSON library and packaged `libtmux-workspace` CLI:

```console
$ cpm install \
    --global \
    LibTmux::Workspace
```

Add [LibTmux-Async](https://metacpan.org/dist/LibTmux-Async) for Future-returning
operations:

```console
$ cpm install \
    --global \
    LibTmux::Async
```

- Companions declare their core dependency; the installer adds it.
- Core and workspace use only the Perl standard library at runtime.
- Async adds Future, IO::Async, IO::Async::Loop::Ppoll and IO::Ppoll. IO::Ppoll
  needs a C compiler.
- Programs that use the packages need no author tools or Python.

The `0.x` API can change between releases. Read each distribution's `Changes`
file before upgrading, and pin versions in applications.

## Prepare a source checkout

Install [Perl](https://www.perl.org/get.html) and
[cpm](https://github.com/skaji/cpm#installation). With mise installed, the
checkout's `.tool-versions` selects its Perl. Clone the repository:

```console
$ git clone https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-perl.git
```

```console
$ cd libtmux-perl
```

If the pinned interpreter is not installed:

```console
$ mise install
```

Check the interpreter selected for installation and execution:

```console
$ mise exec -- perl -v
```

The [contributor setup](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#environment) adds a
hash-verified standalone cpm installer and an isolated author environment.

## Install from the source checkout

With Perl and cpm on `PATH`, install core from the repository root:

```console
$ cpm install \
    --global \
    ./packages/core
```

Add workspace for the JSON library and packaged `libtmux-workspace` command:

```console
$ cpm install \
    --global \
    ./packages/workspace
```

Add async for Future-returning operations:

```console
$ cpm install \
    --global \
    ./packages/async
```

## Run a first program

The [core quick start](../packages/core/examples/quickstart.pl) creates its own
session, splits and resizes a pane, adds a window, captures the graph, and
removes the session. It runs its own tmux server:

```console
$ perl packages/core/examples/quickstart.pl
```

```text
editor: 2 panes
logs: 1 pane
side pane: 20 columns
```

The [examples index](../examples/README.md) lists filtering, concurrent
operations, workspace loading and the author programs.

Installed API documentation uses POD:

```console
$ perldoc LibTmux::Server
```

If something fails:

- **tmux is missing.** Install it, or pass a socket path and the tmux path as
  the example's two arguments.
- **`NoServer` from `snapshot`.** The socket has no daemon; create a session
  with `new_session` first.
- **A session name conflicts.** That is an error; an example never deletes an
  existing session.

---
title: Filter captured selections
description: Native Perl arrays, strict criteria, graph quantifiers, and wire filters.
---

## Query installed objects and ordinary records

Use `where({...})` for query data and `grep(sub ($pane) {...})` for arbitrary
Perl. Native `->@*`, indexing, `grep`, `map`, `sort` and List::Util keep
working; `to_array` returns a fresh unblessed array reference.

[select.pl](../packages/core/examples/select.pl) starts a private server,
splits a window, and filters its panes:

<!-- example: packages/core/examples/select.pl -->
```perl
use v5.44;
use File::Temp ();
use LibTmux::Server;

my $private = File::Temp->newdir('libtmux-perl-XXXXXX', TMPDIR => 1);
my $server  = LibTmux::Server->new(
    socket_path => "$private/tmux.sock",
    config_file => '/dev/null',
);
my $failure;
try {
    my $session = $server->new_session(
        name    => 'perl-select',
        command => [$^X, '-e', 'while (<STDIN>) { print }'],
    );
    my $editor = $session->window_links->one->window;
    $server->rename_window(window => $editor, name => 'editor');
    $server->split_pane(
        pane       => $editor->panes->one,
        horizontal => true,
        command    => [$^X, '-e', 'while (<STDIN>) { print }'],
    );

    my $snapshot = $server->snapshot;
    my $panes =
        $snapshot->windows->one({name => 'editor'})
        ->panes->where({width => {-gte => 1}})
        ->grep(sub ($pane) { $pane->height > 0 });
    my $active = $panes->one({active => true});
    say 'editor panes: ',          $panes->count;
    say 'active pane belongs to ', $active->window->name;

    # example: begin nomatch
    try { $panes->one({width => {-gt => 10_000}}) }
    catch ($error) {
        die $error unless $error isa LibTmux::X::NoMatch;
        say 'no pane is that wide';
    }

    # example: end nomatch
}
catch ($error) { $failure = $error }

# The server is private, so stopping it removes everything the program made.
try { $server->kill_server }
catch ($error) { $failure //= $error unless $error isa LibTmux::X::NoServer }
die $failure if defined $failure;
```

The [record-only program](../packages/core/examples/filters.pl) needs no tmux
server:

```console
$ perl packages/core/examples/filters.pl
```

<!-- example: packages/core/examples/filters.pl#records -->
```perl
use v5.44;
use LibTmux::Filter;

my $filter = LibTmux::Filter->new(
    entity => 'pane',
    where  => {
        active          => true,
        current_command => {-in  => [qw(perl vim)]},
        width           => {-gte => 80},
    },
);
my @records = (
    {id => '%1', active => true,  current_command => 'perl', width => 120},
    {id => '%2', active => false, current_command => 'perl', width => 120},
    {id => '%3', active => true,  current_command => 'vim',  width => 40},
);
my @matches = grep { $filter->matches($_) } @records;
say 'matching records: ', join ', ', map { $_->{id} } @matches;

```

It prints `matching records: %1`. The complete source also checks a JSON round
trip.

## Criteria

Fields select the comparison: text, safe decimal integers, booleans,
nullability, operators and relation cardinality all come from one catalog.

- False, zero, `"0"`, empty text and undef stay distinct.
- Integer operands are bounded to +/-9007199254740991. Invalid numeric text
  never becomes zero.

| Grammar | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| scalar or `-eq`, `-ne` | Schema-directed equality and complement. |
| `-in`, `-not_in` arrays | Explicit membership; empty arrays mean false/true. |
| `-lt`, `-lte`, `-gt`, `-gte` | Authorized numeric ordering. |
| `-contains`, `-starts_with`, `-ends_with` | Literal, case-sensitive text. |
| `-and`, `-or` arrays; `-not` node | Complete criteria nodes. |
| `-some`, `-every`, `-none` | To-many quantifiers over the complete captured domain. |
| `-is`, `-is_not` | To-one criteria or explicit nullable absence. |

- Fields and operators in one hash are conjoined. A duplicate Perl hash key
  overwrites; use several operators or an explicit `-and`.
- Empty criteria and an empty AND are true; an empty OR is false.
- On a loaded empty relation, `-some` is false and `-every` and `-none` are
  true.
- Conditions inside one `-some` apply to the same child; separate existentials
  may match different children.
- An unloaded relation never proves empty.
- Known-null ordering and text are false. Negation reverses known results,
  never a missing-data failure.

## Evaluation order

- Compilation of the whole filter comes before evaluation, even on an empty
  selection. Hash keys traverse in lexical order; logical arrays keep theirs.
- A short circuit may skip an unavailable read once the result is known. For
  an inactive record with unloaded width, an AND testing `active` before
  `width` can return false, and the reverse order throws.
- Flattening those nodes into a hash selects lexical order. Wire serialization
  keeps logical-array order.
- Compilation caps depth at 64 and nodes at 10,000. Membership operands and
  string bytes are uncapped.

## Selections stay mutable

- Native arrays stay mutable, so every library method validates all N members
  before returning, even `first`, `count` or `exists`. That is O(N).
- Predicates may then stop early. `where` validates its output; `iterator`
  also copies membership.
- Raw indexing and dereferencing keep normal Perl behavior.

## Save criteria for reuse

`LibTmux::Filter` owns normalized criteria, matches plain records or
registered readers, and exports JSON with schema `"libtmux.where/v1"`. Wire
names use camelCase and dash-free operators.

<!-- example: packages/core/examples/filters.pl#wire -->
```perl
my $restored = LibTmux::Filter->from_json($filter->to_json);
say 'restored filter matches: ',
    scalar grep { $restored->matches($_) } @records;

```

It prints `restored filter matches: 1`.

- Changing the original criteria hash does not change a compiled filter.
- Schema validation still runs after decoding.
- Regexes, coderefs, cycles and blessed values are refused at the data
  boundary. Native `qr//` works in `grep` callbacks.

## Distinguish one child from two children

One `-some` subtree applies every condition to the same child. Two existential
subtrees can match different children. The workflow limits the domain to its
own editor window and checks both cases. It continues from the workflow's
`$snapshot` and `$editor`:

<!-- example: packages/core/examples/workflow.pl#relations -->
```perl
my $windows    = $snapshot->windows->where({id => $editor->id});
my $same_child = $windows->where(
    {
        panes => {-some => {-and => [{index => 0}, {index => 1}]}},
    }
);
my $different_children = $windows->where(
    {
        -and => [
            {panes => {-some => {index => 0}}},
            {panes => {-some => {index => 1}}},
        ],
    }
);
say 'same child: ',         $same_child->count;
say 'different children: ', $different_children->count;

```

- A pane cannot have index 0 and index 1, so `same child` is 0.
- The window has both panes, so `different children` is 1.
- Loaded empty relations make `-some` false and `-every` and `-none` true.
  Unloaded relations stay errors when evaluation needs them.

See [graph identity](graph.md).

## Conformance fixtures

- A source-pinned Python QueryList evaluator agrees on the shared subset:
  Boolean, integer and text equality, literal contains, prefix and suffix, and
  membership, including empty membership. It does not claim Python accepts
  this wire API.
- Known-null equality differs: the pinned Python filter rejects None fields
  before its equality lookup.
- Numeric ordering, availability errors, graph quantifiers, validation on
  empty data and canonical names have no Python contract. They are marked
  unsupported there, and Perl fixtures cover them.

See [the fixtures](../conformance/where-v1.json) and
[the pin](../scripts/conformance-reference.json).

# Examples

Start with the standalone programs in each distribution. They use installed
public modules and ordinary Perl, with no Python, author fixture or source-tree
library path. They need Perl 5.44 or newer, tmux 3.3a or newer, and Linux.

## Run an installed-package example

[Install core](../docs/installation.md), then run the quick start from a
checkout:

```console
$ perl packages/core/examples/quickstart.pl
```

- It runs its own tmux server, creates and removes its own session, and stops.
- Pass a socket path to join a server you already run. The program then removes
  only its own session and leaves the rest.
- A second argument names the tmux executable.
- A session with the example's name is an error, never a cleanup target.

| Program | Task | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Core quick start](../packages/core/examples/quickstart.pl) | Create, split, resize, rename, capture, clean up, and retain the graph. | `editor: 2 panes`, `logs: 1 pane` and `side pane: 20 columns`. |
| [Select panes](../packages/core/examples/select.pl) | Filter captured panes and handle an empty selection. | `editor panes: 2`. |
| [Send input](../packages/core/examples/input.pl) | Type, capture, set environment and options, and batch commands. | `PROJECT=api` and `@build=ok`. |
| [Explain a query](../packages/core/examples/explain.pl) | Show what tmux runs and what stays local, without tmux. | `tmux filter: ...` and `stays local: ...`. |
| [Retained graph](../packages/core/examples/graph.pl) | Keep an old capture across a rename. | `captured name: logs` and `live name: build`. |
| [Core workflow](../packages/core/examples/workflow.pl) | Arrange windows, filter, compare quantifiers, and verify native queries. | `core workflow: ok`. |
| [Filter records](../packages/core/examples/filters.pl) | Match hash records, round-trip JSON, and inspect validation errors without tmux. | `%1` matches; the invalid numeric operand reports its criterion path. |
| [Async operations](../packages/async/examples/concurrent.pl) | Run concurrent Futures and ordered batches, remove the session, and await close. | `first` before `second`; `async operations and cleanup: ok`. |
| [Workspace loading](../packages/workspace/examples/load.pl) | Plan, load, inspect two windows and three panes, repeat with skip, and clean up. | `workspace plan, load, repeat: ok`. |

Async needs its own distribution and Ppoll dependencies. Workspace needs core
and the workspace distribution. Every program ships with its distribution's
README and logo assets.

## Run repository qualification programs

These programs use the repository's fixture. Provision the
[author environment](../.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#environment) first.
`Future::AsyncAwait` is needed only for `await.pl`.

```console
$ mise exec -- make examples
```

| Program | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| [quickstart.pl](quickstart.pl) | Select contextual window links, filter captured panes, and verify fixture cleanup. |
| [selection.pl](selection.pl) | Arrays, callbacks, cardinality, wire filters, relations, retained graphs, and native verification. |
| [workspace.pl](workspace.pl) | Plan, load, inspect panes, and repeat with `existing => 'skip'`. |
| [async.pl](async.pl) | Capture through a caller-owned Ppoll loop and await cleanup. |
| [await.pl](await.pl) | Use optional caller `async`/`await` syntax with core result objects. |
| [async-lifecycle.pl](async-lifecycle.pl) | Preserve failures, handle cancellation, and observe cleanup without destroying a borrowed server. |

`async-lifecycle.pl` also works with installed packages against an existing
socket. Run its `--help` before `--fail` or `--cancel`. A cancelled operation
does not prove cleanup has finished; keep driving the loop until close
succeeds.

## How the examples are checked

[The runner](../scripts/run-examples.pl):

- Rejects a nonzero exit or missing expected output.
- Runs each live program with an owned private socket and a sentinel session,
  then checks that the program's session is gone and the sentinel remains.
- Runs the self-contained programs with no socket, and fails if one leaves a
  tmux server or files behind.

CI runs the same programs on the oldest and newest supported tmux. The
installed-artifact job extracts the examples from the native archives, checks
them against the source, and runs them from an external installation prefix.

Embedded README and guide blocks marked `example` come from a complete program
or a named region in it. Check for drift:

```console
$ mise exec -- make check-snippets
```

The [shared capability showcase](https://github.com/libtmux/docs/issues/243)
lists only executed examples with recorded CI evidence.

---
title: Explicit acquisition and native filters
description: Explicit acquisition and native filters with the Perl libtmux distributions.
---

## See what runs in tmux and what stays local

- `$snapshot->panes->where($criteria)` and callbacks evaluate in Perl, with no
  I/O.
- `query_panes` acquires a graph and returns a `PaneSelection`.
- `explain_panes` builds a plan with no I/O, using the support-floor tmux
  capabilities. Running a query binds capabilities to the captured daemon.

[explain.pl](../packages/core/examples/explain.pl) needs no tmux server:

<!-- example: packages/core/examples/explain.pl -->
```perl
use v5.44;
use LibTmux::Server;

# Planning does no I/O, so this program needs no tmux server.
my $server = LibTmux::Server->new;

my $criteria = {active => true, width => {-gte => 1}};
my $plan     = $server->explain_panes(where => $criteria);
say 'tmux filter: ', $plan->to_data->{native_filter};

my $relation = {window => {-is => {name => 'editor'}}};
my $residual = $server->explain_panes(where => $relation);
say 'stays local: ', $residual->to_data->{residual_reasons}[0];

my $never = $server->explain_panes(where => $criteria, pushdown => 'never');
say 'pushdown off: ', $never->summary;
```

It prints the tmux filter for the first plan, the reason the second stays
local, and the summary with pushdown off.

## Compare local and native results

The [installed-package workflow](../packages/core/examples/workflow.pl) runs
both on a controlled graph. It continues from the quick start's `$server`:

<!-- example: packages/core/examples/workflow.pl#query -->
```perl
my $where = {active => true, width => {-gte => 1}};
my $local = $server->query_panes(where => $where, pushdown => 'never');
my $verification;
my $verified = $server->query_panes(
    where           => $where,
    pushdown        => 'require',
    on_verification => sub ($report) { $verification = $report },
);
say 'native verification: ', $verification->{status};

```

It prints `native verification: agreed` after checking that both calls return
the same IDs.

| Policy | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `never` | Acquire and evaluate locally. |
| `auto` | Verify safe scalar native candidates; fall back to captured local results on disagreement. |
| `require` | Require complete exact lowering and native/captured agreement. |

- `auto` is the default. It costs one extra command when lowering is
  available. Pick `never` when you only need the captured answer.
- Every policy still acquires and evaluates the complete graph first, so local
  errors stay visible. The native check saves no I/O.
- Either result is a captured local selection.
- A plan lists commands, lowered filters, residual reasons and capability
  needs. Numeric lowering uses tmux numeric expressions, and literal operands
  are escaped for the tmux grammar.

## Read the verification report

Pass `on_verification => sub ($report) { ... }` to inspect the comparison.

- The observer gets one detached hashref, runs inline once after a successful
  decision (including a fallback), and its return value is ignored.
- Its exceptions propagate unless the operation was cancelled; cancellation
  drops later results and errors.
- A failed acquisition, decode or native command never calls it.

The report holds:

- `status`, `comparison`, the capture generation and interval, the executed
  filter, and residual reasons.
- Captured, local and native ID arrays.

Statuses:

- `disabled` means `never`; `local` means nothing could be lowered safely.
- `agreed` separates exact equality from partial candidate inclusion.
- `disagreed` lists missing, unexpected and uncaptured IDs.
- `native` reports only captured membership, for the expert escape hatch.

See [`Server`'s report contract](../packages/core/lib/LibTmux/Server.pm) and the
[tested query example](../examples/selection.pl).

## When native and local disagree

- Under `require`, a disagreement throws `LibTmux::X::QueryMismatch`. The
  report sits under the `verification` key of `LibTmux::X::details`, and the
  observer does not run.
- A mismatch can be a race, a compiler defect or a backend difference; it
  does not say which. Matching results do not prove an atomic capture. [ADR 0003](dev/adr/0003-query-verification-diagnostics.md) records
  the decision.

## What tmux can check

- A partial AND conjunct can prune candidates. A partial OR or NOT cannot.
- Relations, null, bytes and unsupported scalar operators stay local, and a
  complete relation domain is never pruned before `every` or `none` runs.
- Relation pushdown and serialized regexes are deferred.
- `native_filter` is an expert escape hatch, exclusive with portable criteria
  and the pushdown policy. It selects captured root IDs, rejects IDs that
  appeared after capture, and uses native tmux semantics rather than wire
  semantics.

title: Linux compatibility and qualification
description: Linux compatibility and qualification with the Perl libtmux distributions.
---

What is supported:

- **Perl 5.44 or newer.**
- **tmux 3.3a or newer**, including every release after it. Plain tmux 3.3 is
  below the floor.
- **Linux on x86-64, including WSL.** Other systems and ABIs are unqualified;
  the supervisor refuses an unsupported ABI before dispatch.

What CI runs:

- The latest stable Perl, against the oldest and newest supported tmux.
- Releases in between are supported without cells of their own.
- A missing or skipped cell counts as unverified.

[The source lock](../scripts/tmux-lock.json) pins the official tmux sources,
archive hashes, source commits and configure flags. Each build records its
compiler and executable hashes.

Run the compatibility check:

```console
$ mise exec -- make compatibility
```

The oldest supported tmux crashes on an invalid layout name. The `select_layout`
wrapper rejects an unknown or ambiguous name that lacks a custom-layout
checksum prefix before dispatch; the raw `cmd` escape hatch keeps tmux's own
behavior.

---
title: Load a JSON workspace
description: Load a JSON workspace with the Perl libtmux distributions.
---

The separate workspace distribution packages the `libtmux-workspace` CLI.
Validate and plan without tmux I/O; load through public core APIs.

## Describe a workspace

Save [the packaged configuration](../packages/workspace/examples/workspace.json)
as `workspace.json`, or use it from the checkout. Its commands are Perl
programs, with two editor panes and a logs window:

<!-- example: packages/workspace/examples/workspace.json -->
```json
{
  "schema": "libtmux.workspace/v1",
  "environment": {"PROJECT": "api"},
  "sessions": [{
    "name": "perl-workspace",
    "windows": [{
      "name": "editor",
      "layout": "even-horizontal",
      "panes": [
        {"command": ["perl", "-e", "while (<STDIN>) { print }"]},
        {"command": ["perl", "-e", "while (<STDIN>) { print }"], "horizontal": true}
      ]
    }, {
      "name": "logs",
      "panes": [{"command": ["perl", "-e", "while (<STDIN>) { print }" ]}]
    }]
  }]
}
```

- Each pane takes a literal `command` argv or an explicit `shell_command`.
- Environment inherits workspace, session, window, pane. The working directory
  inherits from the window unless overridden.
- Layout applies after splitting.
- The format is versioned JSON; no YAML adapter is selected.

## Run the CLI

From the repository root:

```console
$ libtmux-workspace validate packages/workspace/examples/workspace.json
```

```console
$ libtmux-workspace plan packages/workspace/examples/workspace.json
```

```console
$ libtmux-workspace load packages/workspace/examples/workspace.json \
    --socket-path "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/libtmux-perl-workspace-$$.sock" \
    --existing skip
```

- `load` leaves the workspace running; the CLI has no stop verb.
- `--dry-run` makes a nonmutating plan.
- The default `existing=error` checks every session-name conflict before it
  creates anything.
- `skip` keeps the whole existing session. Repeated loads create only absent
  sessions; this is not reconciliation of an existing layout.
- Exit status: 0 success, 2 usage or configuration, 3 load failure, 4 conflict.

## Load from Perl

The [standalone Perl example](../packages/workspace/examples/load.pl) plans,
loads, checks the graph, repeats with `skip`, and removes its own session. It
runs its own tmux server:

```console
$ perl packages/workspace/examples/load.pl
```

The plan is local and performs no tmux I/O:

<!-- example: packages/workspace/examples/load.pl#plan -->
```perl
use v5.44;
use FindBin;
use LibTmux::Workspace;

open my $in, '<:raw', "$FindBin::Bin/workspace.json" or die $!;
my $json = do { local $/; <$in> };
close $in or die $!;
my $workspace = LibTmux::Workspace->from_json($json);
my $plan      = $workspace->plan;
say 'planned sessions: ', scalar $plan->{sessions}->@*;
die 'plan must not mutate' if $plan->{mutates};

```

It loads and inspects captured public core objects:

<!-- example: packages/workspace/examples/load.pl#load -->
```perl
my $report   = $workspace->load(server => $server);
my $snapshot = $server->snapshot;
$session = $snapshot->sessions->one({name => 'perl-workspace'});
my $windows = $session->window_links;
say 'loaded windows: ', $windows->count;
my $editor = $windows->one({window => {-is => {name => 'editor'}}})->window;
say 'editor panes: ', $editor->panes->count;

```

Repeating with `skip` preserves the whole existing session:

<!-- example: packages/workspace/examples/load.pl#repeat -->
```perl
my $again = $workspace->load(server => $server, existing => 'skip');
say 'skipped existing sessions: ', scalar $again->{skipped}->@*;

```

The program prints one planned session, two loaded windows, two editor panes
and one skipped session.

## Recover from a failed load

- A failed load reports the completed steps, the failed step, the created IDs,
  dispatch uncertainty and cleanup errors.
- Rollback removes only sessions this load proved it created.
- Application readiness needs assertions of your own.
- `LibTmux::Workspace::X::Load->report` keeps each cleanup exception with its
  captured target and attempted action. `cause` stays the original failure; a
  cleanup failure never replaces it.
- `report_data` returns a detached, JSON-safe export with the primary cause and
  the cleanup error classes. Native stdout and stderr use explicit base64
  fields. The CLI prints it on standard error.
